findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] --resume breaks a LIVE lock and can let two writers corrupt the ledger. The resume-only stale-lock break deletes any existing .batch-ledger.lock WITHOUT checking whether the holder process is still alive. Scenario: driver A is still running and holds the lock; driver B starts --resume, removes A's LIVE lock, acquires its own, skips A's already-written records, and appends the rest while A keeps appending too -> duplicate/corrupt ledger, and B may exit 0 before A appends later duplicates. Fix: the stale-lock break must check the holder PID liveness (read the lock's holder.json/pid; break ONLY if the process is dead). A live holder means a genuine concurrent driver -> precondition_failed, not a break.

[codex-host-2, verified] Truncated-tail repair can wrongly drop a VALID final record. repairTruncatedTail truncates the trailing line, but a genuinely complete final record whose line simply lacks a trailing newline (valid JSON, no newline at EOF) would be dropped -> that iterationId becomes a GAP on resume (or a spurious re-run/dup). Fix: only drop the trailing segment if it does NOT parse as valid JSON (genuinely incomplete); if the last line parses cleanly, KEEP it as a complete record. Distinguish 'valid record, no trailing newline' (keep) from 'truncated partial write' (drop).

repairTruncatedTail (run-batch.mjs:182-220) unconditionally drops everything after the last newline when the ledger file does not end with \n, even when that trailing fragment is a COMPLETE, valid, parseable JSON record — contradicting its own documented invariant ("Every COMPLETE prior record is preserved verbatim", line 178; "All well-formed prior lines are honored", line 129-131). Reproduced: a ledger of rec1\n + rec2 (rec2 complete JSON, only missing the trailing newline) has rec2 silently deleted by repairTruncatedTail, so its already-completed iteration is silently discarded and re-run on resume. The single-line branch (lastNl < 0, lines 197-209) DOES check JSON.parse before dropping and preserves a parseable lone line, but the multi-line branch (lines 210-219) drops unconditionally without ever checking whether the trailing fragment parses — an inconsistent/incomplete repair that can discard real evidence though it does not create a duplicate.
